literature_name: Campylobacter concisus and related oral campylobacters
name_note: In GTDB, Campylobacter_A is a split of the classical genus Campylobacter that contains the oral and intestinal species such as Campylobacter concisus, C. curvus, C. rectus and C. showae, not C. jejuni or C. coli.

sentences.text: Campylobacter concisus is described as a bacterium that inhabits human oral cavities and is found in dental plaque, and as a biofilm producer.
A study of children and adolescents with inflammatory bowel disease described C. concisus as an oral commensal and suspected intestinal pathogen, and cultured it from stool and saliva samples.

A report states that metagenome sequencing has linked strains including Campylobacter concisus to Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, and that the role in disease progression remains to be investigated.
The same work identified nineteen indole-containing metabolites produced by C. concisus and assessed their contribution to inflammation.
